sections.title: Maxwell’s Equations: Electromagnetic Waves Predicted and Observed

variables.meaning: the speed of light in a vacuum, the speed at which every electromagnetic wave travels, 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s
the permeability of free space, 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A, the constant that sets the strength of the magnetic force
the permittivity of free space, 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/N·m², the constant that sets the strength of the electric force
the resonant frequency of the RLC circuit Hertz used to generate and to detect his waves
the strength of the electric field of the wave at a point, produced by the charge distribution on the antenna
the strength of the magnetic field of the wave at the same point, produced by the current in the antenna
the speed of light, which is also the ratio of the electric field strength to the magnetic field strength in any electromagnetic wave in a vacuum
the period of the oscillation driving the antenna, which is also the period of the wave it sends out
the frequency of the wave, the frequency at which the charges in the antenna oscillate
the wavelength of the wave, proportional to the period of the oscillation and so shorter at higher frequencies
the speed of an electromagnetic wave in a medium, which is less than the speed of light in a vacuum
the index of refraction of the medium, the factor by which it slows an electromagnetic wave
the speed of light, the propagation speed of every electromagnetic wave in a vacuum
the frequency of the wave, which decides the band of the spectrum it belongs to
the wavelength of the wave, which sets the smallest detail it can resolve and the most efficient length of an antenna
the propagation speed of a wave of any kind, which for an electromagnetic wave in a vacuum is the speed of light
the intensity of the wave, the power it carries through unit area
the average intensity of a continuous sinusoidal electromagnetic wave
the peak intensity of a continuous sinusoidal wave, twice the average intensity
the maximum electric field strength of the wave, its electric amplitude
the maximum magnetic field strength of the wave, its magnetic amplitude
the power the source delivers, which spread over an area gives the intensity
the area the power is spread over
the speed of light, which appears in all three expressions for the intensity
the permittivity of free space, 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C²/N·m²
the permeability of free space, 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A
